**Why now.** This card has sat in `pm:queue` since its filing (2026-09-30T06:07Z), and its third day is due an explicit transition. The previous holder of this seat recorded that it 「waits on the maintainer's own accounts, ⛔ not on a dev」. Read against the scope list, that is true of only part of it:

- **Dev-dispatchable, in this repository** (no external account):

  - item 2's documented Codex `config.toml` snippet, including the `x-api-key` header and `npx mcp-remote` fallbacks, written from the shipped surface.
- **Only the maintainer can act:**

  - item 2's maturity check against a signed-in Codex CLI;
  - the submissions to the official registry, mcp.so, Smithery and PulseMCP, which need the project's accounts.

**Asked of triage, one answer:**
1. Split, or keep whole? If split, a dev-half card (`domain:cli`, p3), and this card going to `pm:awaiting-maintainer` with a `Maintainer-action:` line for the account-bound acts.
2. Whether the dev half is p3 or below, given that NORTH-STAR priority rule 3 holds p2/p3 tool work while this lane has an open p1. #21454 is open at p1 in this lane's queue (under `pm:retriage`).

## Prep for the maintainer's account-bound acts: a live test target, the client settings, and the four listings' text

From the maintainer's local session on 2026-10-12, on the maintainer's instruction 「你能做的你先处理」. Nothing was submitted and no account was used. Every act below stays the maintainer's (ruling `A`, 2026-10-05).

### Test target (live)

- `https://os-4s63kc.objectos.app/api/v1/mcp`: a staging environment, with AI Agent Access switched on for this purpose today.
- Probe results are on objectstack-ai/cloud#786 `6116603565`:
  - protected-resource metadata 200;
  - `POST /api/v1/mcp` → 401 with `resource_metadata`;
  - DCR `registration_endpoint` and PKCE S256 advertised.
- Sign in with the maintainer's own account. The environment's owner is `jack@objectstack.ai`.

### 1. ChatGPT connector

- In ChatGPT settings, enable developer mode, then create a connector:
  - MCP server URL: the test target above;
  - authentication: **OAuth**.
- Expect a redirect to `…/api/v1/auth/oauth2/authorize`, the sign-in page, a consent screen, and then the tool list.
- Record:
  - whether DCR succeeded;
  - which scopes were requested;
  - the tools listed;
  - one read call (for example, list accounts) and its result.

### 2. Codex CLI

- ⚠ **The local install is broken.** `codex` fails with `spawn …/codex-darwin-arm64/vendor/…/codex ENOENT`, so the native binary is missing. Reinstall first: `npm i -g @openai/codex`.
- Then add the server as a remote MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`. The exact key names follow Codex's current docs:
  - a `[mcp_servers.objectstack]` table;
  - `url = "https://os-4s63kc.objectos.app/api/v1/mcp"`.
- Sign in with Codex's MCP OAuth login.
- **Fallback if Codex's remote OAuth is not mature:** an `osk_` API key from the environment's *Connect an Agent* page, sent as the `x-api-key` header, or the `npx mcp-remote` bridge.
- Record which path worked.

### 3. The four metadata-only listings

**Official MCP Registry.**
- `packages/mcp/server.json` on `main` is ready to publish with `mcp-publisher`, after `mcp-publisher login github` as the `objectstack-ai` org:
  - name `io.github.objectstack-ai/objectstack`;
  - one `streamable-http` remote, templated as `https://{host}/api/v1/mcp`;
  - optional `x-api-key` header.
- ⚠ Its `version` reads **`17.6.0`** while `@objectstack/mcp` is **`17.7.0`** on npm and in `package.json`. Bump it to the current release before publishing, because each registry version is immutable.
- `websiteUrl` `https://objectstack.ai/docs/ai/connect-mcp` answers 200.

**mcp.so, Smithery, PulseMCP.** These are web forms on the project's account. Text to paste:

- **Name:** ObjectStack
- **One-liner:** Read and write your ObjectStack app's records and run its actions from any MCP client.
- **Description:**

  > ObjectStack is an open-source, metadata-driven application platform. Every ObjectStack deployment, whether self-hosted or an ObjectOS Cloud workspace, serves an MCP endpoint at `/api/v1/mcp`. Through it, AI assistants can query and update the app's records and run the actions the app exposes. Every call runs as the signed-in user, within their permissions. Sign in with OAuth 2.1 (PKCE, dynamic client registration), or send an API key minted on the deployment's *Connect an Agent* page.
- **Server URL:** `https://<your-deployment-host>/api/v1/mcp`. There is no shared hosted endpoint: each deployment or workspace has its own.
- **Transport / auth:** Streamable HTTP · OAuth 2.1, or `x-api-key`.
- **Links:**
  - docs: `https://objectstack.ai/docs/ai/connect-mcp`;
  - repository: `https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack` (subfolder `packages/mcp`);
  - privacy: `https://www.objectos.ai/en/privacy/`;
  - terms: `https://www.objectos.ai/en/terms/`.
- **Categories:** Productivity / Databases / Developer tools. Licence as in the repository.

⚠ **Shared with objectstack-ai/cloud#786.**
- *Off by default:* every ObjectOS Cloud workspace has AI Agent Access off until an administrator turns it on.
- *No support page:* there is no support contact page yet.

The maintainer's open question today (MCP on by default, or on for paid organisations) decides the first. A listing reviewer who connects a fresh workspace today sees `mcp_not_enabled`.

**Maintainer ruling, 2026-10-12:** 「云服务暂时 MCP 只开给付费版」 (for now, ObjectOS Cloud offers MCP to paid plans only). The motive is the resource cost of agent calls. The change is carried by objectstack-ai/cloud#2765.

Consequences for this card:
- The listing must say that MCP on ObjectOS Cloud needs a paid workspace. OSS self-host is unchanged.
- A reviewer needs a paid workspace to test the connection.
- The staging test target `os-4s63kc` is on `free`. It is moved to a paid plan for the runs once #2765 lands.
